metadata.title: GoFathom — Project Approach 1.1
metadata.status: Debated foundation • proposed design • implementation not audited
metadata.lineage: GoFathom is the new name for SupaBiz. Historical SupaBiz editions remain unchanged.
metadata.purpose: Help a business see what is pending, who owns it, and the evidence behind it; then safely coordinate and verify the next action.
metadata.evidence: 18 bounded project reviews, earlier harness research, and two rounds of Claude critique. Eleven reviews include selected source/client/examples; seven are public-product reviews. No complete vendor security audit, customer validation or new product benchmark is claimed.
metadata.limits: 298 learning entries are candidate observations, not 298 independent validations; they previously used 20 rationale templates. No measured uplift, customer willingness to pay or production readiness is established.
metadata.revision_method: All twelve decisions were critiqued in Claude’s gofathom chat, rebutted by Codex and adjudicated. Agreement is not implementation evidence or customer validation.

debate_summary.status: Three completed critique/rebuttal rounds; no remaining blocking objection from Claude, with explicit Codex qualifications adopted.
debate_summary.reviewer_scope: Claude read canonical JSON core sections at commit 09bd2ac, critique.txt and the repaired synthesis. It inspected the 18 project entries and 76 packages structurally, sampled stage examples/comparisons, and did not re-read all project reports, HTML, diagrams, ZIP or text/JSON parity. This is a document review, not a code audit.

rounds.purpose: All twelve decisions challenged against stages/contracts/roadmap/cost.
Codex rebutted invariants, cancellation, source scope, risk and measurement claims; Claude revised recommendations.
Final qualifications on processing gaps, conservative transmit markers, harmful restrictive instructions, risk assurance and attested values; Claude accepted them.

qualified_or_rejected: One event → one candidate: replaced with revision accounting and many-to-many evidence.
After claim means too late: replaced with fenced before-send marker, conservative unknown outcomes and verified cancellation.
Restrictive instructions are safe: rejected; delay, urgency and consequence remain part of risk.
Canaries alone establish rare-event recall: rejected; known-path tests and natural observations are reported separately.
Natural data alone is mandatory/sufficient for reliance: replaced with an authorized, risk-specific assurance case.
Rank or specificity silently overrides a hold: rejected; explicit override capability/target required.
Opening evidence proves review quality: rejected; use outcome-oriented review exercises and spot checks.
Every linked session has identical scope, or Gmail label selection is provider-enforced: unverified assumptions; inspect each adapter.
No electronic API means no usable evidence: qualified; dated authorized scans/counts/attestations can support limited checks.
A paid commitment must precede discovery: rejected; keep bounded discovery separate from demand and reliance gates.
debate_summary.next_evidence: Actual code audit, permitted source access and real workflow observation. Another AI review cannot substitute for these.
debate_summary.version_applied: Foundation 1.1 incorporates the Codex qualifications and final mechanism additions. Foundation 1.0 stays unchanged.

adjudication.claude_objection: Router-declined messages can disappear from every board lane.
adjudication.codex_response: Accept complete intake accounting; reject one message → one candidate and terminal-only counts.
adjudication.accepted_change: Account for each source revision and workflow evaluation as pending, excluded with reason, quarantined, failed or assessed. Assessed events link to zero or more candidates; candidate matching and work status remain separate. Audit exclusions and replay changed rules.
adjudication.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Reconcile a fixed journal window including pending/failed items. One message creates several candidates; several messages support one candidate; an excluded critical item is found by independent review.

adjudication.claude_objection: The authority system is named in prose, but external edits can invalidate pending decisions.
adjudication.codex_response: Accept C17; observation is bounded by actual connector capability, not a promised universal one-sync guarantee.
adjudication.accepted_change: Bind each authoritative field to a system, source identity/version or hash, read method, observation window, write mode and cutover. Revalidate the bound revision before admission/writeback; external changes stale dependent checks.
adjudication.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Edit a source while review is pending; require re-review. After cutover, conflicting edits to the former authority raise a dual-write exception.

adjudication.claude_objection: An isolated parser may still hold broad database credentials and unrestricted egress.
adjudication.codex_response: Accept worker profiles; differentiate untrusted parsers from trusted ingestion/effect services. Ordinary environment access is not itself a security failure.
adjudication.accepted_change: Untrusted parser gets only the scoped asset, no production secrets or direct database access, restricted filesystem/egress, resource limits and a validated derivative-output API. Trusted workers receive separate least-privilege profiles.
adjudication.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Deny forbidden socket/filesystem/credential access; bound resource exhaustion; allow legitimate derivative submission and inspect quarantined failures.

adjudication.claude_objection: A module name can be mistaken for tested implementation; evidence labels are templated.
adjudication.codex_response: Accept commit-pinned audit rows and divergent entrypoints. Historical par/CC-224 cases are reproduction targets, not asserted fail/pass results.
adjudication.accepted_change: Audit every H/C responsibility with commit, code path or explicit absence, entrypoints, known divergent paths and test artifacts. Distinguish not audited, absent, partial, present-untested and tested-at-commit.
adjudication.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Locate code and permitted fixtures; reproduce historical failures if available. A tested status requires pinned test evidence; the documentation template remains unfilled until then.

adjudication.delivery_gate: Pilot / G1; review before runner expansion
adjudication.claude_objection: A simple runner can grow into an unowned workflow engine.
adjudication.codex_response: Accept a charter and owner; reject an arbitrary one-timer cap, quarterly-only review and automatic Temporal adoption.
adjudication.accepted_change: Register job states, timer types and transitions. Support leases/fences, classified retries, outbox and scoped cancellation. Complex signal graphs, child orchestration or in-flight definition migration trigger a comparative engine spike. Domain effect reconciliation remains required.
adjudication.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Test crash, stale lease, timer, cancellation and upgrade recovery. Review complexity at phase exit and on new primitives or incidents; compare engineering and operating effort.

adjudication.claude_objection: Selected groups may be a filter rather than a restriction at the provider.
adjudication.codex_response: Accept source-enforced versus application-filtered distinctions; inspect the actual adapter instead of assuming all sessions or Gmail labels have identical scopes.
adjudication.accepted_change: Disclose provider-visible scope and selected processing scope separately. Minimize nonselected content before durable capture, including controllable SDK cache/log/crash paths. Assess dedicated number/host, account risk and explicit exposure limits; reject incompatible deployments.
adjudication.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Inject nonselected content in a controlled test and inspect journal, media, traces, cache and crash artifacts. State measured exclusions and unavoidable session exposure; do not promise zero traces without evidence.

adjudication.claude_objection: License checks miss protocol changes, provider terms and account restrictions.
adjudication.codex_response: Accept an owner and fallback for external-service risks. Import success does not prove continuous capture.
adjudication.accepted_change: Dependency records name provenance, rights, capabilities, provider/account constraints, failure owner and fallback mode with actual freshness limits. Only adopt what the chosen workflow needs.
adjudication.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Exercise selected connector recovery and a permitted import fallback; label manual/delayed operation and gaps rather than presenting it as live continuity.

adjudication.claude_objection: Revocation, cancellation and a kill switch are underspecified once a request is in flight.
adjudication.codex_response: Accept C06 policy/grant/epoch and cancellation evidence. Reject after claim = too late and atomic revocation across external systems.
adjudication.accepted_change: Serialize local claims and durable before-send transmit markers with current grant/cancel epochs. A scope stop fences later boundaries. The marker means possible transmission, not success; earlier attempts may need reconciliation. Before-send prevention requires marker/fencing invariants on every path. Compensation is a new authorized action.
adjudication.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Inject revocation/cancel before claim, between claim/send, during send, after remote commit and after lost response. UI only claims prevented/cancelled/completed when evidence warrants it; otherwise unknown.

adjudication.claude_objection: A blanket text-first launch could exclude evidence needed by the chosen photo/voice workflow.
adjudication.codex_response: Accept required modalities per workflow; native-text-first is an extraction preference, not a product restriction. Video remains conditional on need.
adjudication.accepted_change: C16 records required input modalities, language/noise conditions and citation locator types. Use native structure when suitable; process required images/voice from the first selected slice.
adjudication.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Score real permitted media by risk slice, wrong extraction and abstention. Show page/region/time locators where applicable and unsupported coverage explicitly.

adjudication.delivery_gate: Pilot / G2; controls before rule activation
adjudication.claude_objection: Instruction conflict, override, expiry and change-class authority are not explicit.
adjudication.codex_response: Accept semantic fields; reject rank-plus-specificity as a universal override rule and shadow activation as sufficient proof for every high-risk change.
adjudication.accepted_change: Use policy-defined override capabilities, explicit target/supersedes links and scope checks. Hold incompatible unresolved rules. Define timezone/boundary/condition/release authority. Confirmation policy depends on target/risk; ambiguous or consequential changes require exact review.
adjudication.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Cover owner hold versus subordinate release, ambiguous Friday, count-time thresholds, incompatible overlaps and action-in-flight supersession. Use replay/shadow plus protected future-case tests when risk requires.

adjudication.delivery_gate: Pilot / G1 and every reliance expansion
adjudication.claude_objection: Intake cannot be the sole source of its own eligible-event denominator.
adjudication.codex_response: Accept independent inventories with provenance and known shared failure modes. Reject canaries as the only way to estimate rare-event recall or proof of natural-event recall.
adjudication.accepted_change: C10 separates source observation basis, known gaps and processing coverage. C16 identifies independent inventory/eligibility adjudication and denominator status. Report labeled real-event results, synthetic/canary results and unknown unseen coverage separately. Record risk-slice reliance in C18; combine appropriately limited evidence in an authorized assurance case rather than requiring or trusting one evidence type universally.
adjudication.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Drop an event before intake and before routing; the comparison must detect or declare the unobservable gap. Live canaries require explicit consent and isolation from consequential workflows.

adjudication.delivery_gate: Human roles when needed; automated delegation later
adjudication.claude_objection: A CA or authorized operator may serve several businesses before agent exchange exists.
adjudication.codex_response: Accept scoped human roles now; tenant boundaries alone are insufficient and cache clearing is not an authorization mechanism.
adjudication.accepted_change: Give principals independent business/matter grants and explicit active context. Key caches by tenant, principal/grant revision and audience; recheck on reads. Cross-business disclosure is a separately authorized action, including for a common owner.
adjudication.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Switch businesses, revoke one grant and reuse a stale context/cache key; no other business evidence is disclosed. Add automated agent exchange only after a repeated authorized workflow justifies it.

mechanisms.title: Coverage has a basis, not a green promise
mechanisms.mechanism: A source window records the maximum provider scope, selected scope, observed interval, cursor/export/attestation basis, independent inventory provenance and unexplained delta. Processing counts reconcile the captured journal separately. A healthy session supports “observed since”, not proof of every message. Unknown denominators remain unknown.
mechanisms.example: A corrected notice missing before the connector cannot be found by comparing the model to its own journal. A separate permitted inventory may detect the omission; if none exists, the report cannot claim end-to-end recall.
mechanisms.boundary: Counts deduplicate by source identity/revision. Do not count multiple candidate records as multiple ingested messages.

mechanisms.title: Field authority survives external edits
mechanisms.mechanism: An authority binding identifies the external system/ref scheme, read method, observed revision/hash, freshness policy and write mode. A candidate/check binds that revision. A newer authoritative value stales the check; admission/writeback revalidates or stops for reconciliation. Cutover is explicit and former-authority edits are exceptions. Label an attested comparison with the named source and time; never imply it is a live authoritative-system read.
mechanisms.example: The accountant changes a received quantity while an invoice discrepancy awaits approval. The old proposal is stale; accepting it must not overwrite the newer record.
mechanisms.boundary: No change feed or revision token means weaker observation. Use disclosed hash/manual reconciliation and avoid an unearned concurrency guarantee.

mechanisms.title: Cancellation is a protocol, not an undo button
mechanisms.mechanism: A transaction claims an authorized intent against current policy/grant/cancel epochs. A committed scope stop prevents later claims. Every before-send path persists transmit_started_at under current epochs before calling the provider. That marker conservatively means transmission may have occurred, not that it did. A prior stop can prevent the marker; a post-marker missing receipt remains unknown. Verify provider cancellation/completion; separately authorize compensation.
mechanisms.example: An order is claimed, then the owner presses Stop. If no request was sent it may be prevented; if the supplier committed it, GoFathom cannot truthfully label it cancelled without a confirmed cancellation.
mechanisms.boundary: Earlier claims can be in flight. Database atomicity does not extend across an uncontrolled provider. No blind resend after timeout.

mechanisms.title: Instructions need explicit override authority
mechanisms.mechanism: Store target/effect, scope selector, condition, issuer capability, stated/recorded/confirmed/effective times, timezone, expiry boundary, release condition, conflict set and explicit supersedes/override policy. Neither a newer timestamp nor a narrower instruction automatically defeats a hold. Ambiguity is held for a precise clarification. Instructions skipping confirmation must match an explicit tenant policy entry; show known affected work and due dates before consequential activation.
mechanisms.example: A staff member says “credit note received, pay” while the owner’s supplier hold is active. Evidence of a credit is not authority to release the hold.
mechanisms.boundary: Low-risk explicit authenticated instructions may use pre-agreed confirmation rules. Consequential or ambiguous changes require exact review; models cannot choose a weaker change class to bypass controls.

mechanisms.title: Review capacity is visible operational state
mechanisms.mechanism: The queue shows risk, age, owner, SLA, pending volume and estimated effort. A review budget forecasts capacity; overflow triggers a backup reviewer/escalation and a visible backlog, not automatic acceptance or concealment. Batch only equivalent bounded proposals and bind every confirmation to its targets.
mechanisms.example: Ramya has 20 notices awaiting review. The brief reports pending/unreviewed items and coverage even when the planned daily review budget is exhausted.
mechanisms.boundary: Opening evidence is not proof of thoughtful review. Use disclosed simulation exercises, spot checks and correction/outcome quality; diagnostic telemetry is not employee scoring.

mechanisms.title: A bounded runner with an accountable owner
mechanisms.mechanism: Before live operation, name a runner owner and register job states, legal transitions, timer types, lease/fencing behavior, retry classes, outbox, cancel and version policy. Pin in-flight jobs to a supported definition; unknown versions are held. New orchestration primitives require a comparative engine review rather than unreviewed expansion.
mechanisms.example: A proposed child workflow plus cross-job signal graph exceeds the initial charter. Compare an established engine under the same failure suite before extending the runner.
mechanisms.boundary: Domain reconciliation is mandatory and may run as a bounded job; it is distinct from building a generic compensation framework. Ownership is a required pilot field, not a currently assigned person.

mechanisms.title: Trust boundaries differ by worker
mechanisms.mechanism: Define parser, inference, intake and effect capability profiles. A parser receives one scoped asset and a validated output channel; no production DB credentials, sensitive environment secrets or unrestricted network. Apply resource/time limits. Intake and effect workers have different narrowly scoped capabilities and auditable purposes.
mechanisms.example: A PDF tries to fetch a URL or read a secret file. Its parser has neither the authority nor the credentials; legitimate derivative output still succeeds.
mechanisms.boundary: Isolation has to be demonstrated for the actual runtime. Merely using a container or calling a worker isolated proves nothing.

mechanisms.title: Discovery has frozen terms and honest evidence
mechanisms.mechanism: Version and digest the pilot’s source window, eligible-event definition, comparison arms, risk slices, modalities, review burden, thresholds, price experiment and stop conditions before scoring. Amendments retain history and require a fresh comparable window. Observe baseline time where feasible and label self-report limitations. Record each authorized reliance decision in C18 with evidence versions, residual risks, review date and fallback.
mechanisms.example: A late rule change would improve apparent recall by excluding hard notices. Keep the original score and run a separately versioned comparison instead of moving the denominator.
mechanisms.boundary: A paid commitment is stronger than a friendly verbal yes but is neither a prerequisite for bounded discovery nor proof of product-market fit. Unknown prices remain unknown.

test_registry.title: Captured-event conservation
test_registry.stimulus: Replay one source revision twice; leave another pending; quarantine one; exclude one with a rule; let one message create three candidates and a burst support one candidate.
test_registry.expected: Captured source revisions reconcile once across pending/excluded/quarantined/failed/assessed states. Candidate links are many-to-many; no excluded event disappears from audit.

test_registry.title: Independent denominator and canary limits
test_registry.stimulus: Remove an eligible event before journal capture and another at routing; compare a separately sourced inventory. Include shared-failure and unknown-inventory variants.
test_registry.expected: Report observed omission or unknown denominator. Labeled real-event recall and known canary detection are separate; processing reconciliation alone never proves source completeness.

test_registry.title: Authority revision conflict
test_registry.stimulus: Change an external field after a check is proposed and before admission/writeback; edit the former authority after cutover.
test_registry.expected: Stale bound check cannot authorize overwriting the new value. Re-read/review or reconcile; dual-authority edits raise a visible exception.

test_registry.title: Revoke and cancel at each boundary
test_registry.stimulus: Revoke before claim, after claim/before send, during send, after remote commit and after lost receipt; race two dispatchers.
test_registry.expected: No claim after committed scope stop. Earlier claims receive truthful prevented/requested/verified-cancelled/completed/unknown labels. At most one valid local claim per intent generation; provider effects reconciled.

test_registry.title: Unknown effect and compensation
test_registry.stimulus: Provider commits then times out; a retry arrives; later compensation is requested.
test_registry.expected: No blind duplicate action; reconcile first. Compensation requires its own current authorization and receipt. Unknown is never silently relabeled failed or cancelled.

test_registry.title: Instruction semantics and override
test_registry.stimulus: Apply a supplier hold; propose narrower subordinate release; use “until Friday” without boundary; supersede after dispatch claim.
test_registry.expected: Unauthorized release and ambiguous boundary are held. Explicit authorized overrides trace their target; prospective rules do not undo an already emitted effect. A model cannot invent a preauthorized instruction policy entry; affected-work preview names its coverage limits.

test_registry.title: Review backlog and exact confirmation
test_registry.stimulus: Exceed planned review capacity; submit two similar proposals; issue an ambiguous “OK”.
test_registry.expected: Backlog and age remain visible, escalation has an owner and nothing auto-accepts. Ambiguous confirmation binds to no proposal until clarified. Critical work is not hidden by budget caps.

test_registry.title: Runner charter and upgrade
test_registry.stimulus: Crash after lease claim; run a stale worker; restart a timer; deploy an unknown job definition; request a new unsupported orchestration primitive.
test_registry.expected: Fence stale worker, preserve bounded timer/retry progress, hold unsupported definitions and trigger a runner/engine review. Reconcile effect uncertainty outside retry guessing.

test_registry.title: Parser boundary and source minimization
test_registry.stimulus: Attempt prohibited file/network access and resource exhaustion; inject nonselected chat content into a controlled adapter fixture; inspect storage/log/cache/crash paths.
test_registry.expected: Permitted derivative still works; prohibited access is denied. Document actual prefilter exposure and measured persistence. Reject a deployment whose agreed privacy boundary cannot be met.

test_registry.title: Frozen experiment and model qualification
test_registry.stimulus: Change eligibility after results, swap model/parser, use unavailable observer and expose oracle answers to acting model.
test_registry.expected: Original results remain; amended experiment has new digest/window. Model swap reruns qualified cases; unobservable episode is ungradable; oracle leakage invalidates evaluation. A changed or expired reliance decision prevents expansion of the allowed automation scope.

test_registry.title: Human multi-business isolation
test_registry.stimulus: A CA/operator switches businesses, reuses a cached result and then loses one grant; try sharing under a common owner.
test_registry.expected: Active context and current scoped grants govern reads/exports; cache key and invalidation cannot substitute for authorization. Cross-business disclosure needs an explicit allowed purpose.

test_registry.title: Required modalities and citations
test_registry.stimulus: Feed permitted blurred photo, noisy Hinglish audio, text-only email and sampled video as required by the chosen workflow.
test_registry.expected: Return supported cited candidates or visible uncertainty; modality coverage and wrong-extraction/abstention reported per risk slice; no unsupported hidden-condition inference.

runner_charter.owner: Unassigned — must be named before live pilot
supported: Registered job states and legal transitions
Declared bounded timer types per workflow
Classified bounded retry and dead-letter/review outcome

Recovery/cancellation incidents or growing operational toil

runner_charter.boundary: Choose the simplest implementation that passes the same recovery/cancellation/version suite. Review does not automatically select Temporal. Domain effect reconciliation remains mandatory.

changes.title: Same 12 stations; Foundation 1.0 intact
changes.reason: The factory structure and platform vision remain. The new edition refines mechanisms and delivery gates; it does not turn every responsibility into pilot scope.

changes.title: Two different coverage checks
changes.reason: Independent inventory versus received events measures observed source coverage. Received revisions versus processing dispositions measures conservation. Unknown denominators and aged processing backlog stay visible.

changes.title: C17: authority per field
changes.reason: Name authority, external identity/version, observation health, write mode and cutover. New external edits stale dependent proposals and checks.

changes.title: Cancellation before and after transmission
changes.reason: A durable transmit marker is evidence of possible transmission, not proof of it. Serialize local fencing; reconcile outside effects and use evidence-backed UI labels.

changes.title: Instruction semantics and review capacity
changes.reason: Explicit override authority, scope, time boundaries and change classes; consequential holds are not automatically safe. Backlogs escalate rather than silently auto-accept.

changes.title: Runner and worker capabilities
changes.reason: An owned versioned runner charter limits custom infrastructure. Parser, intake and effect workers have distinct enforced capability profiles.

changes.title: Vendor cost, customer burden and combined cost
changes.reason: Customer time is not automatically a vendor cash expense. Model three views, count subscription as a transfer in combined economics, and label price assumptions.

changes.title: Debate, provenance and untested implementation
changes.reason: A twelve-decision log, declarative failure registry, code-audit template and source-path index show what changed, why and what has not been demonstrated.

decisions.title: Begin with an evidence-led work board
decisions.choice: Account for each source revision and workflow evaluation as pending, excluded with reason, quarantined, failed or assessed. Assessed events link to zero or more candidates; candidate matching and work status remain separate. Audit exclusions and replay changed rules.
decisions.why: Owners and coordinators need a reliable next step, owner and supporting source, not another disconnected conversation.
decisions.alternative: A universal personal assistant maximizes breadth; a narrow exception board makes missed work, review load and completion measurable.
decisions.revisit_when: A paid pilot demonstrates demand for adjacent workflows and enough shared semantics to add them.
decisions.proof: Reconcile a fixed journal window including pending/failed items. One message creates several candidates; several messages support one candidate; an excluded critical item is found by independent review.
decisions.claude_objection: Router-declined messages can disappear from every board lane.
decisions.codex_response: Accept complete intake accounting; reject one message → one candidate and terminal-only counts.

decisions.title: Keep a single authority for each field
decisions.choice: Bind each authoritative field to a system, source identity/version or hash, read method, observation window, write mode and cutover. Revalidate the bound revision before admission/writeback; external changes stale dependent checks.
decisions.why: A second ungoverned stock or financial ledger creates disagreements that an agent cannot resolve by confidence.
decisions.alternative: Marble suggests richer operational records; Definite suggests exact reconciliation. Take both patterns but explicitly name the owner of each quantity and status.
decisions.revisit_when: A customer authorizes a scoped migration with opening balance, cutover, reconciliation and rollback.
decisions.proof: Edit a source while review is pending; require re-review. After cutover, conflicting edits to the former authority raise a dual-write exception.
decisions.claude_objection: The authority system is named in prose, but external edits can invalidate pending decisions.
decisions.codex_response: Accept C17; observation is bounded by actual connector capability, not a promised universal one-sync guarantee.

decisions.title: Use a modular application with isolated workers
decisions.choice: Untrusted parser gets only the scoped asset, no production secrets or direct database access, restricted filesystem/egress, resource limits and a validated derivative-output API. Trusted workers receive separate least-privilege profiles.
decisions.why: A small team can trace a transaction and deploy coordinated contracts without paying for 12 service boundaries.
decisions.alternative: One always-running VM per customer offers continuity but adds idle cost and secrets exposure. Independent services add operational overhead before load is measured.
decisions.revisit_when: Measured queue contention, isolation requirements or independent release cadence justify a split.
decisions.proof: Deny forbidden socket/filesystem/credential access; bound resource exhaustion; allow legitimate derivative submission and inspect quarantined failures.
decisions.claude_objection: An isolated parser may still hold broad database credentials and unrestricted egress.
decisions.codex_response: Accept worker profiles; differentiate untrusted parsers from trusted ingestion/effect services. Ordinary environment access is not itself a security failure.

decisions.title: Keep the useful harness; make models replaceable
decisions.choice: Audit every H/C responsibility with commit, code path or explicit absence, entrypoints, known divergent paths and test artifacts. Distinguish not audited, absent, partial, present-untested and tested-at-commit.
decisions.why: The research does not prove the current harness should be rewritten or that every model behaves equivalently.
decisions.alternative: Hermes supplies agent-loop patterns; an entire personal-agent product does not supply business grants or accepted records.
decisions.revisit_when: A measured quality, cost or maintainability gap remains after bounded fixes.
decisions.proof: Locate code and permitted fixtures; reproduce historical failures if available. A tested status requires pinned test evidence; the documentation template remains unfilled until then.

decisions.codex_response: Accept commit-pinned audit rows and divergent entrypoints. Historical par/CC-224 cases are reproduction targets, not asserted fail/pass results.

decisions.choice: Dependency records name provenance, rights, capabilities, provider/account constraints, failure owner and fallback mode with actual freshness limits. Only adopt what the chosen workflow needs.
decisions.why: Public source is not proof of compatibility, license rights or production safety.
decisions.alternative: Executor may reduce integration work; adopting it wholesale does not replace exact-action approvals and reconciliation.
decisions.revisit_when: Unresolved rights, security fixes or excessive maintenance cost require an alternative.
decisions.proof: Exercise selected connector recovery and a permitted import fallback; label manual/delayed operation and gaps rather than presenting it as live continuity.
decisions.claude_objection: License checks miss protocol changes, provider terms and account restrictions.
decisions.codex_response: Accept an owner and fallback for external-service risks. Import success does not prove continuous capture.

decisions.title: Deterministic authorization outside AI
decisions.choice: Serialize local claims and durable before-send transmit markers with current grant/cancel epochs. A scope stop fences later boundaries. The marker means possible transmission, not success; earlier attempts may need reconciliation. Before-send prevention requires marker/fencing invariants on every path. Compensation is a new authorized action.
decisions.why: A persuasive explanation or independent reviewer model cannot create authority.
decisions.alternative: Decawork inspires contextual review; hard rules still decide absolute denies. Human approval cannot make false evidence true.
decisions.revisit_when: New action classes require new schemas, grants and tests, not broader system prompts.
decisions.proof: Inject revocation/cancel before claim, between claim/send, during send, after remote commit and after lost response. UI only claims prevented/cancelled/completed when evidence warrants it; otherwise unknown.
decisions.claude_objection: Revocation, cancellation and a kill switch are underspecified once a request is in flight.
decisions.codex_response: Accept C06 policy/grant/epoch and cancellation evidence. Reject after claim = too late and atomic revocation across external systems.

decisions.title: Progressively richer media
decisions.choice: C16 records required input modalities, language/noise conditions and citation locator types. Use native structure when suitable; process required images/voice from the first selected slice.
decisions.why: Most business value comes from preserving source evidence and asking the right small clarification, not processing every frame.
decisions.alternative: Sidekick supports worker-friendly capture; Shire suggests continuous observation. Start with user-supplied evidence before ambient monitoring.
decisions.revisit_when: A measured workflow needs video temporal coverage or optional local capture and accepts its cost and consent boundary.
decisions.proof: Score real permitted media by risk slice, wrong extraction and abstention. Show page/region/time locators where applicable and unsupported coverage explicitly.
decisions.claude_objection: A blanket text-first launch could exclude evidence needed by the chosen photo/voice workflow.
decisions.codex_response: Accept required modalities per workflow; native-text-first is an extraction preference, not a product restriction. Video remains conditional on need.

decisions.title: Govern change according to impact
decisions.choice: Use policy-defined override capabilities, explicit target/supersedes links and scope checks. Hold incompatible unresolved rules. Define timezone/boundary/condition/release authority. Confirmation policy depends on target/risk; ambiguous or consequential changes require exact review.
decisions.why: Fast operational control and trustworthy improvement have different lifecycles.
decisions.alternative: Asakana inspires correction UX; GrepAI suggests tested procedures. Neither establishes that automatic self-training is appropriate.
decisions.revisit_when: Impact scope expands, a formerly benign alias affects financial/matter identity, or rollback proves insufficient.
decisions.proof: Cover owner hold versus subordinate release, ambiguous Friday, count-time thresholds, incompatible overlaps and action-in-flight supersession. Use replay/shadow plus protected future-case tests when risk requires.
decisions.delivery_gate: Pilot / G2; controls before rule activation
decisions.claude_objection: Instruction conflict, override, expiry and change-class authority are not explicit.
decisions.codex_response: Accept semantic fields; reject rank-plus-specificity as a universal override rule and shadow activation as sufficient proof for every high-risk change.

decisions.title: One portable evaluation contract
decisions.choice: C10 separates source observation basis, known gaps and processing coverage. C16 identifies independent inventory/eligibility adjudication and denominator status. Report labeled real-event results, synthetic/canary results and unknown unseen coverage separately. Record risk-slice reliance in C18; combine appropriately limited evidence in an authorized assurance case rather than requiring or trusting one evidence type universally.
decisions.why: Two overlapping evaluation platforms would fragment the definition of success.
decisions.alternative: Hue helps manage episodes and comparison; Rystic helps simulate stateful dependencies. Neither owns the business oracle.
decisions.revisit_when: A purchased capability has proven fidelity, rights, data controls and lower total operating burden.
decisions.proof: Drop an event before intake and before routing; the comparison must detect or declare the unobservable gap. Live canaries require explicit consent and isolation from consequential workflows.
decisions.delivery_gate: Pilot / G1 and every reliance expansion
decisions.claude_objection: Intake cannot be the sole source of its own eligible-event denominator.
decisions.codex_response: Accept independent inventories with provenance and known shared failure modes. Reject canaries as the only way to estimate rare-event recall or proof of natural-event recall.

decisions.title: Defer cross-business agents and native capture
decisions.choice: Give principals independent business/matter grants and explicit active context. Key caches by tenant, principal/grant revision and audience; recheck on reads. Cross-business disclosure is a separately authorized action, including for a common owner.
decisions.why: Agent-to-agent transport does not prove business completion or authorize sharing.
decisions.alternative: Agent Relay enables communication; the customer relationship, minimal evidence and verification protocol remain ours.
decisions.revisit_when: Two customers need a repeated shared workflow with demonstrated value and permitted data transfer.
decisions.proof: Switch businesses, revoke one grant and reuse a stale context/cache key; no other business evidence is disclosed. Add automated agent exchange only after a repeated authorized workflow justifies it.
decisions.delivery_gate: Human roles when needed; automated delegation later
decisions.claude_objection: A CA or authorized operator may serve several businesses before agent exchange exists.
decisions.codex_response: Accept scoped human roles now; tenant boundaries alone are insufficient and cache clearing is not an authorization mechanism.

stages.name: Join & establish trust
stages.question: Who owns this workspace?
stages.purpose: Create a customer and business boundary before granting access. Signup is required for GoFathom; the saved reviews do not establish every vendor’s signup implementation.

parts.name: Account & sign-in
parts.deliverable: Maintained identity provider, sessions and recovery.

parts.name: Business workspace
parts.deliverable: Organization, outlets or chambers, and verified ownership.

parts.name: People & roles
parts.deliverable: Invitations, membership, manager/staff/CA roles and removal.

parts.name: Consent & boundaries
parts.deliverable: Explain selected access, purposes, retention and who sees what.

parts.name: Device enrollment
parts.deliverable: Register a phone/browser; bind optional desktop sessions to a principal.

stages.outputs: Workspace ID, memberships and initial access policy.
stages.gate: A user in Consu cannot read ForeFathers by switching an ID; removed members lose access.
stages.loop: Membership changes return here; account deletion has its own retention/export process.

examples.varun: Varun creates separate Consu and ForeFathers business scopes; staff and CA receive different roles.
examples.ramya: Arkaj creates the chamber workspace; Ramya can coordinate matters without unrestricted access for every staff member.

comparisons.approach: Inkbox contributes stable agent identity and conversation-bound authority; that is narrower than a complete business signup system.
Executor separates account connections from agent use; study that boundary after identity is established.
Agent37 contributes a recognizable personal agent workspace and continuity across devices; hosted tenancy is not audited.
Glen makes shared context ownership relevant; SupaBiz must own membership and source access rules.

gofathom.title: Identity before awareness
gofathom.mechanism: Create the owner account with a maintained identity provider; verify business ownership and invite roles. Keep business scopes separate even when an owner owns both. Staff need a capture/acknowledgment flow; managers get review and assignment; CA gets explicitly shared accounting material.
gofathom.ux: The signup screen explains what will be read, who can see it and how to disconnect. Do not ask for every permission on first launch.

stages.name: Connect permitted sources
stages.question: What may the system access?
stages.purpose: Connect only the accounts and groups needed for a workflow. Reading, sending, exporting and acting are separate capabilities.

parts.name: Connection broker
parts.deliverable: OAuth/session credentials stored outside model context.

parts.name: Source enrollment
parts.deliverable: Choose Gmail inboxes, WhatsApp groups and permitted app scopes.

parts.name: Capability map
parts.deliverable: Describe actual read/write/media/history limits per adapter.

parts.name: Connection health
parts.deliverable: Expiry, missing scopes, reconnect and coverage indicators.

parts.name: Revocation path
parts.deliverable: Disconnect credentials, stop jobs and invalidate affected context.

stages.inputs: Workspace identity, user consent and provider credentials.
stages.outputs: Scoped connection IDs and a verified capability/coverage record.
stages.gate: Reconnect safely; never treat a quiet disconnected source as up-to-date. Existing WhatsApp group access remains an adapter validation task.
stages.loop: Expired access returns here; queued actions recheck permission before dispatch.

examples.varun: Enroll Consu’s operations group and a separate accountant group. Give the pilot read access before enabling reviewed sends.
examples.ramya: Connect Arkaj’s court inbox; scope which attachments and matter records staff may receive.

comparisons.approach: Executor centralizes integrations and credentials so multiple agents can use authorized connections.
Inkbox distinguishes quiet conversation intake, selective activation and the audience of each conversation.
screenpipe adds local screen/audio awareness, with capture controls; this is a later optional source, not a required connector.
Agent37 demonstrates environment continuity and browser handoff; that does not establish durable WhatsApp intake.
Definite’s read-oriented connection pattern is useful before allowing consequential writes.

gofathom.title: Every connector has a coverage contract
gofathom.mechanism: Distinguish maximum provider-visible scope from selected processing scope and record which boundary is provider-enforced versus application-filtered. Inspect the actual adapter, session/cache/log behavior and recovery owner. Minimize nonselected content before durable capture where controllable; disclose unavoidable exposure and reject incompatible deployments. Imports are delayed/manual fallbacks, not proof of live completeness.
gofathom.ux: Show Connected / Catching up / Gap / Reconnect needed. Never show a green complete state merely because authentication succeeded.

stages.name: Understand the business
stages.question: What do these names and messages mean?
stages.purpose: Build an explicit, owner-reviewed business map. Context must be inspectable and corrected; it is not a hidden personality profile. Initial sync already uses stations 05–07 while this business map is being built.

parts.name: Entity directory
parts.deliverable: People, outlets, suppliers, assets, clients and matters with stable IDs.

parts.name: Vocabulary & aliases
parts.deliverable: Map Hinglish names, supplier abbreviations, SKUs and matter-number variants.

parts.name: Audience map
parts.deliverable: Define which group, role or matter can see each kind of evidence.

parts.name: Source authority
parts.deliverable: Assign authoritative sources per field and preserve disagreements.

parts.name: Baseline review
parts.deliverable: Approve opening stock, active matters and known operating constraints.

stages.inputs: Permitted history, owner answers, source documents and existing business lists.
stages.outputs: Versioned business map with explicit unknowns and source provenance.
stages.gate: Ambiguous “the kitchen” or a repeated matter number produces clarification, not a confident wrong match.
stages.loop: Corrections and new entities update this map through review; revoked evidence cannot remain universal context.

examples.varun: Learn which kitchen, refrigerator, supplier and unit belong to Consu. Confirm opening stock rather than inferring it from chat.
examples.ramya: Map court, jurisdiction, case number, parties and staff responsibility; the same number in different courts is not one matter.

comparisons.approach: Asakana demonstrates domain mapping from messy orders into structured business entries; backend training methods remain unknown.
Marble contributes supplier/item/unit and inventory semantics, with ordering and receiving treated separately.
Praxis organizes work around matters, documents and responsible people.
Glen contributes scoped retrieval, memory ownership and provenance, not a universal business ledger.
Definite stresses aligning meaning before comparing records; exact checks need comparable quantities and periods.
Shire adds physical locations and floor context for observation-driven work; defer camera-specific mapping.

gofathom.title: Context is reviewed business data
gofathom.mechanism: Build stable entity IDs, scoped aliases, source-authority rules and a small business vocabulary. Preserve unknowns and disagreements. Consu versus Concu is an unresolved alias, not a merge instruction. Intake and interpretation may run during onboarding.
gofathom.ux: Ask a focused clarification: “Which outlet does this fridge belong to?” Show why the question matters and preview the mapping.

stages.name: Define success & rules
stages.question: What counts as correctly completed?
stages.purpose: Configure one workflow pack with valid states, responsibilities, approval thresholds and measurable outcomes before letting agents act.

parts.name: Workflow pack
parts.deliverable: Typed states, commands, responsibilities and allowed transitions.

parts.name: Approval policy
parts.deliverable: Define allow, deny, hold and human-review rules by action and scope.

parts.name: SOP & knowledge versions
parts.deliverable: Keep draft, tested and active guidance separate.

parts.name: Reference scenarios
parts.deliverable: Protected expected outcomes, forbidden effects and representative ambiguity.

parts.name: Activation & cutover
parts.deliverable: Owner-approved pilot scope, read-only shadowing and rollback plan.

stages.inputs: Reviewed business map, owner objectives and risk boundaries.
stages.outputs: Versioned workflow/policy pack plus a pilot acceptance suite.
stages.gate: A bad workflow or overly permissive rule must fail tests before it becomes active.
stages.loop: Station 12 proposes changes here; no silent self-modification.

examples.varun: Define who can assign a maintenance issue, what proof closes it, and when a purchase needs Varun’s approval.
examples.ramya: Define matter routing, reviewed hearing/deadline types and who may approve changes or share documents.

comparisons.approach: GrepAI turns repeated work into procedures, with a useful distinction between drafts and tested active behavior.
Hue contributes repeatable cases and outcome-based release comparisons.
Rystic contributes stateful practice worlds, fault injection and deliberately broken controls.
Decawork contributes action review in business context; hard grants still belong outside a review model.
Asakana inspires corrections that improve later handling, but SupaBiz must design and test the learning mechanism.

gofathom.title: Define reliance before automation
gofathom.mechanism: Choose one workflow pack and current system of record, buyer, eligible-event definition, expected completion proof and reviewer. Pre-agree source coverage, risk-specific miss limits, review budget, escalation and stop conditions. Record operational instructions separately from model changes.
gofathom.ux: Offer a small responsibility: “Track receiving discrepancies for this outlet.” Explain which actions remain proposals and which may execute.

stages.name: Receive & remember events
stages.question: Did we capture and account for the observed revisions?
stages.purpose: Record permitted source events durably before acknowledging them. Decide whether an event needs work without calling an LLM for every message.

parts.name: Durable inbox
parts.deliverable: Persist source identity, timestamps and raw event envelope.

parts.name: Sync & backfill
parts.deliverable: Cursors, reconnect, initial sync and coverage gaps.

parts.name: Deduplication & revisions
parts.deliverable: Native IDs, edits, deletes, order and replay rules.

parts.name: Wake router
parts.deliverable: Mentions, event rules and bounded bursts select eligible work.

parts.name: Media fetch & quarantine
parts.deliverable: Fetch references safely; isolate untrusted or unknown sources.

stages.inputs: A new message, email, attachment, upload or approved device observation.
stages.outputs: Durable event ID and queued processing job, or a recorded no-action decision.
stages.gate: Captured revisions reconcile across all processing states, zero-candidate outcomes are auditable, aged work is visible, and source completeness is not claimed from internal conservation alone.
stages.loop: Disconnections route to station 02; recoverable failures retry from the journal.

examples.varun: A staff member sends “freezer leaking again” with a photo and a follow-up voice note. Capture the burst as evidence before deciding.
examples.ramya: A court email arrives twice and is later corrected. Preserve both source identity and revision history.

comparisons.approach: Inkbox’s quiet capture and selective wake-up are strong fits for busy WhatsApp groups.
Asakana accepts messy operational messages and attachments as business input.
Sidekick keeps frontline capture in familiar voice/photo/message interactions.
screenpipe is a different intake modality: selected computer activity rather than a business messaging connector.
Shire begins with camera observations; the same intake principles apply, but camera support is optional.

gofathom.title: Persist first, wake selectively
gofathom.mechanism: Persist stable source revisions before advancing checkpoints. Per evaluation version, account for pending, excluded-with-reason, quarantined, failed and assessed revisions. Assessed revisions link zero or more candidates; zero-candidate results need reasons, sampling and replay. Separately reconcile against independent inventories where available. Aged pending items are processing gaps; unseen source events require independent evidence or an unknown denominator.
gofathom.ux: A receipt says captured, not understood or completed. Sync gaps and quarantined attachments appear in the coverage view.

stages.name: Read, hear & see evidence
stages.question: What does the source actually say?
stages.purpose: Extract observations from text, documents, voice, photos and sampled video. Keep source evidence, coverage and uncertainty visible.

parts.name: Evidence storage
parts.deliverable: Original media and derived files with independent retention.

parts.name: Document/OCR pipeline
parts.deliverable: Isolated parsing, page regions and extraction provenance.

parts.name: Speech & language
parts.deliverable: Transcription with language, translation and timestamp separation.

parts.name: Vision/video adapter
parts.deliverable: Scoped image analysis or video sampling with coverage limits.

parts.name: Evidence locators
parts.deliverable: Citations, confidence limitations and useful abstention.

stages.inputs: Durable event and authorized original media.
stages.outputs: Observations linked to page, crop, timestamp or message evidence.
stages.gate: Noise, missing pages or an unclear quantity yields a useful question; sampled video never becomes proof of unseen events.
stages.loop: Missing evidence returns to intake or asks the authorized person for clarification.

examples.varun: Transcribe Hinglish kitchen audio and identify the visible leak. Do not infer internal freezer temperature from a photograph.
examples.ramya: Extract the notice’s matter identifier and date with page citations; distinguish publication date from hearing date.

comparisons.approach: Sidekick combines frontline voice and visual reports with operational context.
screenpipe illustrates an accessibility/text-before-OCR capture ladder and evidence-linked history.
Shire turns visible camera observations into operational signals; hidden conditions remain unknown.
Asakana turns messages and document/photos into structured candidates for review.
Praxis emphasizes documents as part of a matter’s readiness and work context.

gofathom.title: Interpret into cited candidates
gofathom.mechanism: Preserve original assets and derive OCR, transcript or sampled frames with page/time spans and processor versions. Treat messages, PDFs and web pages as untrusted content; their embedded instructions cannot grant tools. Use deterministic code for calculations and pass the computed values plus inputs into the model.
gofathom.ux: Show the photo region or transcript span beside the proposed quantity, date, asset or issue. Ask one targeted question for ambiguity.

stages.name: Form & check business records
stages.question: Which facts can enter the system?
stages.purpose: Separate observations from candidate records and accepted facts. Exact business checks run before admission; uncertainty is a valid result.

parts.name: Typed records
parts.deliverable: Issues, stock movements, invoices, matters and tasks with schemas.

parts.name: Entity resolution
parts.deliverable: Match IDs, aliases and context without merging ambiguous entities.

parts.name: Deterministic checks
parts.deliverable: Exact units, quantities, duplicate references and rule versions.

parts.name: Record admission
parts.deliverable: Version-checked transaction, revision history and outbox.

parts.name: Scoped retrieval views
parts.deliverable: Search/memory projections with provenance and invalidation.

stages.inputs: Observations, business map, existing records and applicable rules.
stages.outputs: Accepted revision, rejected candidate or an unresolved check requiring evidence.
stages.gate: Unknown is not pass; an approval cannot rewrite a false quantity or erase contrary evidence.
stages.loop: Clarification returns to stations 03/06; new evidence can revise an accepted record while preserving history.

examples.varun: Create one freezer issue linked to Consu and the asset. In receiving, only accepted quantities create stock movements.
examples.ramya: Match the email to the correct court and matter, or hold it for Ramya; retain both original and corrected notice.

comparisons.approach: Definite contributes a shared record model, exact checks and explicit unresolved outcomes.
Marble distinguishes order, receipt, invoice, credit and settlement; one generic record cannot replace them.
Terse contributes stable entity ownership and guarded mutations; use SQL as the baseline rather than adding a second authority.
Glen contributes permission-aware retrieval and memory lineage; retrieval stays derived from authoritative records.
Asakana makes a structured draft and targeted correction the bridge from messages to business records.

gofathom.title: Review missing and uncertain items too
gofathom.mechanism: Keep matching, admission and processing status separate; many messages can support one record and one message can yield several records. C17 binds each authoritative field and observation revision. New external edits stale checks; admission/writeback revalidates. Unavailable evidence yields CANNOT_VERIFY. Review queues show risk, age, owner, backup and escalation; no overflow auto-acceptance.
gofathom.ux: A proposed record has old/new values, source, uncertainty and Accept / Correct / Hold. Unmatched items remain discoverable instead of disappearing.

stages.name: Plan & assign the work
stages.question: Who does what, by when?
stages.purpose: The agent proposes bounded next steps. A durable workflow owns assignment, waiting and progression across devices and model calls.

parts.name: Bounded agent loop
parts.deliverable: Context selection, tool schemas, budgets and checkpoints.

parts.name: Durable workflow owner
parts.deliverable: Persist states, timers and recoverable steps.

parts.name: Assignment & acknowledgement
parts.deliverable: Responsible person, acceptance and reassignments.

parts.name: Deadline & escalation
parts.deliverable: Durable reminders, blockers and escalation recipients.

parts.name: Role-specific work views
parts.deliverable: Staff task list, manager attention queue and owner summary.

stages.inputs: Accepted record, current grants, workflow state and SOP version.
stages.outputs: Proposed assignment or action with explicit intent, dependencies and owner. Internal state changes also enforce current permissions.
stages.gate: Sending an assignment is not acceptance; reminders survive worker restarts without duplicate tasks.
stages.loop: Blocked work asks for evidence or reassignment; long waits do not keep a model process running.

examples.varun: The manager gets a short issue card and assigns a responsible person; missing location prompts one focused question.
examples.ramya: Ramya reviews the matter and assigns the right staff member with the notice, date type and expected work product.

comparisons.approach: Praxis contributes matter-centered coordination, document readiness and clear responsibility.
Sidekick turns frontline reports into operational work with location and follow-up.
herdr’s attention inbox and durable job identity inspire a manager view, though its implementation serves engineering agents.
Agent37 contributes continuity across devices and visible outputs.
GrepAI contributes reusable guarded procedures for repeatable work.
Terse’s short guarded commands and committed views are useful without keeping slow model work inside mutations.

gofathom.title: A commitment has an owner and a next step
gofathom.mechanism: An accepted issue or reviewed matter can produce proposed work with assignee, required acknowledgment, due-date source, blockers and completion criteria. During shadowing these are suggestions; the current human process remains authoritative.
gofathom.ux: Today shows needs review, waiting on someone and overdue work. Acknowledge, reassign and explain a blocker without navigating a project-management suite.

stages.name: Authorize the exact action
stages.question: May this action happen now?
stages.purpose: Every consequential action crosses a policy gate. Low-risk permitted actions may pass automatically; review is conditional, not a mandatory click for every event.

parts.name: Current permission check
parts.deliverable: Principal, resource, audience and destination checked at dispatch.

parts.name: Intent & approval digest
parts.deliverable: Bind decision to exact action, record revision and policy version.

parts.name: Decision inbox
parts.deliverable: Allow/deny/hold/needs-context with evidence and changed fields.

parts.name: Budget & limit reservation
parts.deliverable: Reserve allowed spend/quotas before concurrent execution.

parts.name: Expiry & revocation
parts.deliverable: Expire stale approval and re-review changed inputs.

stages.inputs: Exact proposed action, current record versions, grants and limits.
stages.outputs: Authorized intent or denied/held proposal with a reason.
stages.gate: Changed payload, authority revision, policy or grant invalidates the relevant approval. Scope stops fence later claims/transmit markers; earlier possible effects remain visible and are reconciled.
stages.loop: Held actions return to context/review; no model may override a hard deny.

examples.varun: An internal task may be allowed automatically. A supplier order needs the correct business, amount and approver.
examples.ramya: Sharing a notice must use the right matter audience; a revised hearing date is reviewed before changing downstream calendars.

comparisons.approach: Decawork puts action review outside the acting agent and recognizes missing-context/hold outcomes.
Executor provides approval/credential boundaries to study; the saved review records an approval-consumption race requiring a spike.
Inkbox contributes audience binding and approval tied to the actual proposal.
Definite separates factual checks from approval decisions; approval does not make inconsistent evidence true.
Terse contributes current-version guarded commands; stale state must not authorize an effect.

gofathom.title: Bind approval to exactly what changes
gofathom.mechanism: Authorize the exact action against current grants, audience, policy, object/authority revisions and limits. Bind approval to intent and atomically claim it. Serialize grant/cancel epochs again at the durable before-send marker; the marker permits possible transmission, never proves provider success. A scope stop blocks new authorized boundaries and exposes work already in flight.
gofathom.ux: Review cards show the exact action, destination, changed fields, evidence and downstream consequences; batch only equivalent bounded actions.

stages.name: Execute through scoped tools
stages.question: Can we do it safely and recover?
stages.purpose: Execute authorized intent through typed adapters. Use a scoped browser only when a supported API is insufficient and the workflow permits it.

parts.name: Tool gateway
parts.deliverable: Typed input/output, adapter version and scoped credential injection.

parts.name: Effect ledger
parts.deliverable: Idempotency key, attempt identity and before/after state.

parts.name: API & browser execution
parts.deliverable: Restricted worker, egress, destinations and browser handoff.

parts.name: Retry & cancellation
parts.deliverable: Classify pre/post-commit errors; stop the exact worker.

parts.name: Delivery & delegation
parts.deliverable: Audience-safe notifications; job-scoped agent handoff later.

stages.inputs: Authorized intent with an idempotency key and short-lived execution scope.
stages.outputs: Provider receipt, confirmed failure or uncertain outcome requiring reconciliation.
stages.gate: Timeout after a possible provider commit never enters blind resend. Marker/cancel races, bypass attempts and stale workers produce truthful outcome states.
stages.loop: Unknown effects go to station 11; reauthorization is required if the intended action changes.

examples.varun: Create the internal task and send the permitted notification. Store the provider receipt separately from task completion.
examples.ramya: Attach the reviewed notice to the assigned work; update a calendar only under the approved date and audience scope.

comparisons.approach: Executor contributes bounded tool execution and integration/credential separation; SupaBiz owns business effect semantics.
Agent37 illustrates browser/environment handoff; persistent hosting is a separate service decision.
Agent Relay provides communication transport and job-scoped rooms; delivery does not prove business completion.
Inkbox contributes communication adapters, cancellation and distinct receipt/delivery stages.
herdr contributes node/job control patterns; terminal injection is not the restaurant transaction interface.

gofathom.title: Execute once in business terms, reconcile uncertainty
gofathom.mechanism: Each attempt persists transmit_started_at before the external network call on an enforced, fenced path. Before the marker, a committed stop can prevent transmission; after it, missing receipts remain unknown even when no call occurred. Attempt provider cancellation only if supported and verify it. Claim alone is not proof of “too late”; compensation is another authorized action. API/browser workers share this boundary.
gofathom.ux: Pending / Sent / Outcome unknown are distinct. Browser handoff explains what the user must complete and preserves the job identity.

stages.name: Verify, reconcile & close
stages.question: Did the intended result happen?
stages.purpose: Check real outcomes and missing effects before reporting success. Maintain the difference between delivered, acknowledged, completed and verified.

parts.name: Outcome observer
parts.deliverable: Read back provider state or collect domain-specific completion evidence.

parts.name: Reconciliation queue
parts.deliverable: Resolve unknown outcomes, missing receipts and contradictions.

parts.name: Business closure rules
parts.deliverable: Define valid proof and who can accept the completed work.

parts.name: Audit & projections
parts.deliverable: Append result history and refresh scoped dashboards/search.

parts.name: Owner feedback
parts.deliverable: Show outcome, evidence, remaining blockers and meaningful summaries.

stages.inputs: Attempt ledger, provider receipts, worker updates and new evidence.
stages.outputs: Verified completion, confirmed failure, partial completion or unresolved outcome.
stages.gate: A successful tool response cannot close a real-world task without its required evidence.
stages.loop: Failures retry only after reconciliation; changed facts return to station 07 and unresolved work to station 08.

examples.varun: A follow-up photo and manager check close the visible leak task. Invoice discrepancies remain exceptions for the CA.
examples.ramya: Acknowledged assignment is distinct from a filed document; proof of filing is required for that task’s closure.

comparisons.approach: Sidekick contributes verified operational closure rather than stopping at report creation.
Marble contributes receiving/invoice/credit reconciliation before settlement.
Definite contributes evidence-based checks and useful unresolved states.

gofathom.title: Improve through explicit change classes
gofathom.mechanism: Classify changes by target and impact using trusted application rules; models can suggest, not lower controls. One-off fixes, explicit instructions, tenant rules and product changes have different release paths. Overrides need capability and explicit targets; harmful delays count as risk. Use replay, shadow and protected future cases as appropriate, with frozen prospective evaluation terms and separately labeled exploratory rescoring.

contracts.name: Source observation
contracts.rule: Every captured source revision has an accountable processing disposition per workflow evaluation version: pending, excluded-with-reason, quarantined, failed or assessed. Assessed zero-candidate outcomes need reason codes and exclusion-equivalent audit/replay. Multiple candidates may share evidence and one event may create multiple candidates. Preserve revision history, dedupe and checkpoint atomicity. Processing assessments are a separate versioned relation keyed by source identity/revision, workflow pack and evaluation version; do not overwrite one shared source disposition across workflows.

contracts.name: Evidence asset / derivative
contracts.rule: Originals stay immutable. OCR, transcripts, sampled frames, thumbnails and redactions are derived objects with provenance. Signed access is short lived and scoped. Apply BP05/BP06 to issued links and authorized removal; immutable does not mean stored forever.

contracts.name: Candidate and admission decision
contracts.rule: Candidate matching (matched/ambiguous/unmatched), admission and processing state are distinct. The source assessment links zero or more candidates; zero-candidate results require an auditable reason. Admission binds current record and authority revisions; stale or conflicting evidence returns for review.

contracts.name: Business record revision
contracts.rule: GoFathom owns its accepted revisions and decisions; external authoritative fields remain explicitly bound through C17. Revalidate a proposal’s authority revision before admission/writeback. New external edits stale dependent checks; without safe version/readback support, disable automatic writeback and use reviewed reconciliation. Corrections preserve history and trace downstream effects.

contracts.name: Grant and delegation
contracts.rule: Check current principal, business/matter, audience and exact action. Serialize the local dispatch/transmit-intent boundary against grant and cancel epochs. A committed revocation prevents later authorized boundaries; already-transmitting effects may still finish and must be reconciled. Historical disclosure cannot be undone by deleting a cache.

contracts.name: Action intent and receipt
contracts.rule: Persist and fence claim/attempt identity. Before each external network attempt, durably mark transmit_started_at under current grant/cancel epochs; this means transmission MAY have occurred. Absence supports prevented-before-send only when marker-before-send is enforced on every path and stale workers cannot bypass it. After the marker, loss of a receipt means unknown even if the call never happened. Cancellation labels are prevented_before_send, requested, externally_cancelled_verified, completed_or_too_late_verified or unknown; compensation is a separately authorized action. No blind retry of a potentially committed effect.

contracts.name: Task / matter / schedule
contracts.rule: During shadowing the existing human process remains authoritative. After scoped cutover, authority is explicit per field. Assignments need acknowledgment and completion evidence; proposed dates remain distinct from reviewed dates. Review capacity is a planning constraint: overflow is visible and escalated, never automatic acceptance or concealment.

contracts.name: Workflow and outbox
contracts.rule: One runner owns progression. Commit domain changes with outbox intent and dedupe consumers atomically. Register states, transitions and timer types; fence leases and bound retries. In-flight jobs remain on supported definitions; unsupported versions are held. Any migration or charter expansion is explicitly reviewed and recorded. Domain effect reconciliation remains required.

contracts.name: Run / evaluation record
contracts.rule: Trace payloads are minimized and redacted. A release report distinguishes known tests, held-out tests, fault tests and real-pilot observations. Model scores are not authoritative business labels.

contracts.name: Projection freshness and coverage
contracts.rule: Separate SOURCE observation coverage from PROCESSING conservation/freshness. Inventory versus received revisions measures observable source gaps; received versus pending/excluded/quarantined/failed/assessed measures processing accounting. Aged pending work violates its processing SLA even when counts balance. Session-observed, export-reconciled and attested evidence have different limits; a healthy cursor alone never proves complete intake. Unknown denominators prohibit precise end-to-end recall/completeness claims.

contracts.name: Check and reviewed exception
contracts.rule: PASS/FAIL/CANNOT_VERIFY is separate from approval and job completion. Bind current internal and authoritative external input revisions. Unavailable, unobservable or stale required evidence yields CANNOT_VERIFY or an explicitly stale check, never an invented discrepancy. An authorized dated scan/count/attestation can be evidence with stated freshness/limits; no API does not mean no possible evidence.

contracts.name: Scoped correction and governed procedure
contracts.rule: A one-off correction is not standing policy. Classify change and future impact before selecting review, regression, holdout and release gates. Confirmed operational instructions use C15; high-impact tenant-only rules still need strong testing. Record rollback and effects already emitted.

contracts.name: Evaluation world and oracle
contracts.rule: Isolate each mutable world; protect the oracle; failed observations mean ungradable, not pass. No production credentials or endpoints.

contracts.name: Relationship and delegated job
contracts.rule: Later capability: transport identity does not confer authority. Each business retains independent grants; minimum evidence crosses the boundary.

contracts.name: Declared operational instruction
contracts.rule: The issuer must have authority for the target and override. Explicit supersedes/override references and policy-defined relations govern conflicts; narrower scope, recency or job title alone never defeats a hold. Default activation is confirmation time, or explicit authenticated intent acceptance time when a pre-agreed low-risk policy permits it; no automatic backdating. Ambiguous times or incompatible instructions are held. Restrictive effects can cause serious delay: urgency, duration, scope, reversibility and consequence govern confirmation. High-risk tenant changes may need protected future-case tests in addition to replay/shadow diffs. Any direct instruction that skips a second confirmation must match an explicit tenant policy entry, not a model’s runtime guess. Preview known work/due dates affected by a hold and disclose limits of that dependency view.

contracts.name: Pilot and reliance contract
contracts.rule: Freeze pilot terms before confirmatory scoring: sources/windows, denominator, risk slices, modalities, thresholds, review workload and reliance boundaries. Amend with version/digest and disclose results already seen; new thresholds govern prospective confirmatory claims. Retrospective exploratory rescoring is allowed only as labeled analysis, never untouched holdout evidence. Each risk slice needs an authorized reliance decision; insufficient assurance keeps the existing human process authoritative. Canaries, labeled real observations and unknown unseen coverage are reported separately. Paid commitment is a demand signal, not a prerequisite for bounded discovery or proof of product-market fit. C18 stores each authorized reliance decision with evidence, residual risks and review date.

contracts.name: Field authority and cutover binding
contracts.rule: Write mode is none, propose or controlled-write-after-cutover. State which system owns each field, how a value is observed and which revision/hash is bound. Recheck before admission/writeback; source changes stale downstream checks. If observation or safe versioned writeback is unavailable, show CANNOT_VERIFY as appropriate and keep automatic writeback off. Manual dated evidence is possible but its limitations must be explicit. A former authority edited after cutover creates a dual-write exception, not an automatic merge. Label attested/manual values with source and time, distinct from live system-of-record observations.

contracts.name: Authorized reliance decision
contracts.rule: A designated authorized person records whether a specific workflow/risk slice may be relied on, using evidence components, consequence analysis, limitations and residual risks. Insufficient assurance retains the existing human process. Natural observations, protected/fault tests and known-path probes have distinct limits; agreement between AI reviewers is not a validation component. Material source/model/policy changes trigger review; expired or revoked decisions cannot expand automation.
